subject: english-language
title: Selling with Words
welcome_lead: Adverts use language to sneak past your defences.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on advertising techniques.
final_note: You can now spot ad techniques and explain their effect.

concepts.def: Short memorable phrase for a brand.

walkthroughs.body_html: A slogan ('Just Do It') is short, memorable and tied to the brand. Often uses alliteration or rhyme.
Bandwagon says 'join the crowd'. Celebrity endorsement borrows a star's trust to sell. Both are social-proof tricks.
A call to action ends the advert: 'Visit today', 'Sign up now'. Without it, persuasion stalls.

What is the difference between free and bound morphemes?
options: Free morphemes are nouns and bound morphemes are verbs.
Text types are arbitrary and have no patterns.
Free morphemes are free to use and bound morphemes cost money to use.
Free morphemes can stand alone as words ('cat', 'happy', 'run'); bound morphemes must attach to another morpheme (prefixes, suffixes — 'un-', '-ness', '-ing').

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a dialect and an accent?
options: Dialect and accent mean the same thing.
A dialect is a foreign language; an accent is how locals speak.
Free morphemes are nouns and bound morphemes are verbs.
Accent refers only to pronunciation; dialect includes vocabulary and grammar as well as pronunciation — so all dialects involve accents but not vice versa.

mcqs.q: Why do text types have predictable features?
options: Conventions develop because they serve communicative purpose — a recipe needs imperatives because it instructs; a news report needs the inverted pyramid because of how readers scan.
Text types have fixed features just because tradition says so.
Free morphemes are nouns and bound morphemes are verbs.
Text types are arbitrary and have no patterns.
